+
+Cover IDs are formatted as exactly ten decimal digits. The first four digits
+identify an archive.org item (a one million ID range), and the next two
+identify a zip batch (a 10,000 ID range). For example, cover `8,012,345`
+becomes `0008012345`, item `covers_0008`, batch `01`, and zip
+`items/covers_0008/covers_0008_01.zip`. Its filename inside the zip is
+`0008012345.jpg`. The three resized copies use item/zip prefixes `s_`, `m_`,
+and `l_` and filenames `0008012345-S.jpg`, `0008012345-M.jpg`, and
+`0008012345-L.jpg`. All zips are stored without compression so archive.org can
+serve individual files directly at URLs such as
+`https://archive.org/download/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_01.zip/0008012345-S.jpg`.
+
+`archive.archive(test=False)` packages local covers starting at ID 8,000,000.
+It marks rows `archived=true` only after all four variants are in their zips.
+The `filename*` columns continue to point at local images and `uploaded` stays
+false during staging, so requests remain readable. Missing variants set
+`failed=true`; repair them before retrying. Batch locks prevent two archive
+processes from writing the same zip concurrently.
+
+For a staged batch, call `Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True,
+finalize=True)`. This uploads missing zips and checks that all four named zips
+exist in their archive.org items. A failed check returns false and keeps local

+# Cover archive layout and lifecycle
+
+Cover IDs are formatted as exactly ten decimal digits. The first four digits
+identify an archive.org item (a one million ID range), and the next two
+identify a zip batch (a 10,000 ID range). For example, cover `8,012,345`
+becomes `0008012345`, item `covers_0008`, batch `01`, and zip
+`items/covers_0008/covers_0008_01.zip`. Its filename inside the zip is
+`0008012345.jpg`. The three resized copies use item/zip prefixes `s_`, `m_`,
+and `l_` and filenames `0008012345-S.jpg`, `0008012345-M.jpg`, and
+`0008012345-L.jpg`. All zips are stored without compression so archive.org can
+serve individual files directly at URLs such as
+`https://archive.org/download/s_covers_0008/s_covers_0008_01.zip/0008012345-S.jpg`.
+
+`archive.archive(test=False)` packages local covers starting at ID 8,000,000.
+It marks rows `archived=true` only after all four variants are in their zips.
+The `filename*` columns continue to point at local images and `uploaded` stays
+false during staging, so requests remain readable. Missing variants set
+`failed=true`; repair them before retrying. Batch locks prevent two archive
+processes from writing the same zip concurrently.
+
+For a staged batch, call `Batch(item_id, batch_id).process_pending(upload=True,
+finalize=True)`. This uploads missing zips and checks that all four named zips
+exist in their archive.org items. A failed check returns false and keeps local
+images and database paths intact. A successful check updates all eligible
+`filename*` columns to their download URLs, sets `uploaded=true`, then removes
+the local images and staged zips. Repeating this call is safe; completed rows
+retain their remote URLs. Use `test=True` to check without changing state.
+
+Older tar and offset references remain readable for historical covers. They
+are not used for new archival batches.
